I have finally resolved the issue. It wasn't starship prompt at all (: It was antivirus software. It has real-time protection and it's triggered by starship and powershell binaries each time new prompt has to be displayed. The most tricky part is that you have to exclude two binaries from those checks:
- C:\ProgramData\chocolatey\bin\starship.exe;
- C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7\pwsh.exe

Excluding just starship.exe doesn't help even though `Measure-Command { starship explain` starts to show great timings. Remember to exclude pwsh.exe also!

I managed to shave off 1000ms the startup by generating the init code and pasting it directly into my Powershell profile. That way it doesn't need to regenerate the init code on every startup.

```pwsh
# Generate the init code
starship init powershell --print-full-init
```

Just an fyi for anyone that finds this issue.   Frequently the problem is not starship, but rather your anti-virus or zscaler.   I was personally experiencing a 1s delay after prompts due to our companies zscaler and its dlp.   We are still working to address the issue internally.

> The most tricky part is that you have to exclude two binaries from those checks

This helped immensely with Windows Defender, along with changing initialization to:

    starship init powershell --print-full-init | Out-String | Invoke-Expression

IMHO all of this should be documented clearly in the installation instructions.

PS: Starship may be installed with WinGet or other methods. One shall run `Get-Command starship` in order to know what executable should be added to the AV exclusions.

For those having whitelisting issues, the problem may be out of your control if corporate IT is not receptive to whitelisting.

I’ve found success switching to another cross-platform prompt styler that has just as many integrations, and have not had slow startup issues for the past half year. I occasionally still start up starship to check if corporate relaxed its controls but to no avail.

Anyway this’s just my 2 cents since the issue wasn’t going away for me.
